items.title: Problematic if choice of arbitrators can predict arbitration outcome: Justice Indu Malhotra
items.summary: It is deeply problematic if one can predict the outcome of an arbitration based on the composition of the arbitral tribunal, former Supreme Court Justice Indu Malhotra recently said. Justice Malhotra raised concerns over party-appointed arbitrators acting as partisans and warned against predictable decisions in multi-member tribunals. “That is something which I feel is a very serious matter of concern, because if you can predict the result from the constitution of the tribunal, it is problematic,” she said. She was speaking at a panel session during the India ADR Week 2026 in Mumbai. The discussion focused on conflicts, repeat appointments, and perceptions of bias. Advocates put forth the cause of the parties, and arbitrators should not be doing that, she opined. “You cannot expect the arbitrators to be taking a partisan view. They are not required to advocate the cause of the party. That is what I think is the biggest challenge to arbitration today,” she emphasised. Indu Malhotra She further remarked that partisan arbitrators fail their primary mandate. "You cease to be an arbitrator and adjudicator. You cannot be advocating the cause of the party,” the judge said. This is why disclosure by arbitrators about conflict of interest becomes important, she opined. Justice Malhotra praised India's mandatory statutory disclosure framework and urged foreign jurisdictions to adopt similar statutory requirements. The panel discussion was moderated by JSA Partner Farheed Karachiwala . The panel also featured Sherina Petit , Partner and Head of International Arbitration at Stewarts, and Pavani Reddy , Legal Director at Clyde & Co. Petit defended repeat appointments of arbitrators as something driven by genuine expertise. “Principally, if you're good at what you do, the parties are going to want you again,” she said. “What you don't want is a one-hit wonder!” she added. On navigating potential conflict issues, she offered a practical rule: “The test is, when in doubt, disclose." Sherina Petit Reddy contrasted English and Indian legal frameworks. She explained how English courts rely on an objective 'fair-minded observer' test rather than rigid statutory schedules. Pavani Reddy Karachiwala noted that India's 2015 statutory reforms were years ahead in codifying key disclosure standards. “Fairness and neutrality is something which really needs to stand out right on top in any arbitration," he said.

items.title: Madhya Pradesh High Court slams its IT wing for non-functional website; directs audit by TCS, Infosys, L&T
items.summary: The Madhya Pradesh High Court has ordered action against its Information Technology wing (IT wing) staff over repeated glitches in the court's website, which was hampering the Court's functioning, particularly e-hearing. In an order passed on September 8, a bench of Justices Vivek Agarwal and Avanindra Kumar Singh noted that the condition of the website was far from satisfactory and the Court's judicial time was being wasted due to the incompetence of the IT staff. Hence, it directed the Chief Justice to take action against the concerned IT staff. "The High Court Website is not support e-hearing. There are several glitches in the website. We have requested Mr. KS Kushwaha, Registrar (ITCSA) to assist us. He is reported to be on his way to the Court. However, we take a very serious view that our judicial time has been wasted due to incompetency of the IT staff. Let Hon'ble the Chief Justice take action against the concerned IT staff," the Court said. Justice Vivek Agarwal and Justice Avanindra Kumar Singh Further, the Court also ordered the Registrar of IT at the High Court to conduct a detailed enquiry into the roadblocks to the Court's smooth functioning and submit a report within seven days. "Let a detailed enquiry be conducted and reasons be furnished by Shri K.S. Kushwaha as to why obstacle is being caused to the working of the High Court. Action be taken against the delinquent and matter be reported to this Bench within seven days from today," the Court ordered. Pertinently, the Court also directed that an expert team from Tata Consultancy Services (TCS)/Infosys/L&T Technology Services to carry out an audit of the IT system at the High Court. items.title: SNG & Partners advises on inaugural investment by HDFC Capital - Hulic joint debt platform
items.summary: SNG & Partners has advised on the first investment deployed through the joint senior secured debt platform established by Hulic Co., Ltd., in collaboration with HDFC Capital Advisors Limited. The investment was effected by way of subscription to unlisted, secured, non-convertible debentures. SNG & Partners acted as the legal counsel to the investors and the debenture trustee, and has engaged in the drafting, reviewing, and negotiation of transaction documents and also on the cross-border aspects involved in the transaction. Amit Aggarwal (Managing Partner – Corporate & Non-Contentious Practice) provided strategic inputs on the transaction with Aditya Vikram Dua (Partner, Head of Financial Services), Aniket Sawant (Associate Partner), Kartikeya Rao (Associate) and Sonali Nagariya (Associate) forming the core transaction team. The Platform has been set up to provide senior secured debt financing for residential housing development projects in India. This inaugural transaction involves a marquee residential development project located in Western Mumbai. items.title: TTD raises pilgrims’ accident cover to Rs 10 lakh, adds Rs 2 lakh life insurance
items.summary: The Tirumala Tirupati Devasthanams (TTD) Board has approved a free life insurance cover of Rs 2 lakh for pilgrims who die of natural causes while visiting Tirumala, with the amount to be paid to their families. The TTD Board approved the proposal at its meeting in Tirumala on Wednesday, September 9, headed by chairman BR Naidu and attended by executive officer M Ravichandra. Naidu said the initiative would be the first of its kind among temple trusts in the country. Under the proposed scheme, the family of a pilgrim who dies of natural causes during their pilgrimage in Tirumala will receive Rs 2 lakh. TTD will bear the insurance premium. The initiative expands TTD’s existing accident insurance assistance for pilgrims. The Board also decided to increase the compensation for families of devotees who die in accidents in Tirumala from Rs 3 lakh to Rs 10 lakh. The existing assistance covers devotees killed in road accidents between Alipiri and Tirumala under specified circumstances. The decisions come ahead of the annual Salakatla Brahmotsavams of Lord Venkateswara, scheduled from September 15 to 23, when Tirumala is expected to see a substantial increase in the number of devotees. The TTD has projected a 15–20% increase in footfall during Garuda Seva compared to last year. It has also made arrangements to serve annaprasadam to 9.30 lakh devotees during the festivities, compared to the 6.13 lakh last year. The celebrations will begin with Ankurarpanam on September 14, followed by Dwajarohanam on September 15. Chief Minister N Chandrababu Naidu is scheduled to offer silk garments to Lord Venkateswara on September 15 and participate in the Pedda Sesha Vahana Seva. Apart from the pilgrim insurance measures, the TTD Board approved several other proposals ahead of the Brahmotsavams. It sanctioned Rs 1.60 crore over three years towards transport charges for additional sanitation personnel and decided to seek government approval for 400 additional outsourcing workers to augment laddu production during peak demand. The TTD has planned a buffer stock of 10 lakh laddus a day during the Brahmotsavams. The Board also approved a proposal from Indian Oil Corporation Limited (IOCL) to establish a biogas plant to process food waste generated at the Annaprasadam complex, canteens, and hotels in Tirumala. items.title: Decade after Praja Sankalpa Yatra, YSRCP chief Jagan announces another march in 2027
items.summary: YSR Congress Party (YSRCP) president and former Andhra Pradesh chief minister YS Jagan Mohan Reddy has announced a statewide padayatra in September or October of 2027. Scheduled two years ahead of the next Assembly elections, the padayatra is expected to strengthen the party’s grassroots organisation and help it return to power in 2029. Addressing YSRCP leaders, elected representatives and key functionaries from the Parchur Assembly constituency at the party’s central office in Vijayawada on Wednesday, September 9, Jagan called on the cadre to prepare for the upcoming local body elections. He described them as a test of the party’s organisational strength. The proposed padayatra comes nearly a decade after Jagan’s 3,648-km Praja Sankalpa Yatra, which began in November 2017 and continued for 341 days across Andhra Pradesh. He travelled through 13 districts and 134 Assembly constituencies, meeting people and holding public meetings as he positioned himself as an alternative to Telugu Desam Party’s N Chandrababu Naidu. The yatra became a major part of Jagan’s campaign for the 2019 Assembly elections. The YSRCP went on to win 151 of the 175 Assembly seats, paving the way for Jagan to become chief minister. Jagan described the 2029 elections as a “Kurukshetra Sangramam” and said people had already begun examining the current TDP-led administration against the previous YSRCP government. He also expressed apprehension over the conduct of the forthcoming local body elections under the TDP-led government. Referring to the proposed 34% reservation for Backward Classes, he claimed the move could face legal hurdles. He also raised concerns over the ongoing Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls and allegations of voter deletions, saying these developments had created doubts over the manner in which the local body elections would be conducted. He alleged that the ruling establishment was using police pressure, criminal cases, arrests, inducements, and administrative measures to weaken political opponents. The TDP has rejected such allegations. Jagan nevertheless asked party workers to contest the local body elections with determination and extend support to those seeking posts such as sarpanch, Mandal Praja Parishad Territorial Constituency (MPTC) member, and ward member. “Whenever and however elections are held, YSRCP will stand with the people.
